annotations.keyFindings: Adoption of isolation, footbath and visitor measures is patchy; tailored advice and a trusted vet help; few interventions were evaluated and most relied on farmer report.
annotations.limitations: Heterogeneous studies; self-reported practices; mostly temperate regions.

annotations.keyFindings: Thirty-four percent of herds that bought cattle isolated them for three weeks; lack of housing and labour were the main reasons for not doing so.
Facilitated planning with three agreed farm-specific priorities increased observed adoption by 2.1 of 12 measures against 0.8 with usual advice at 12 months; visits took about 2.5 hours.
annotations.limitations: Four practices; no follow-up beyond 12 months; practices volunteered.

annotations.keyFindings: Farmers ignore generic lists but act on two or three priorities agreed with their own vet, especially after seeing disease nearby.
Isolation of purchased cattle was reported on 61 percent of farms but observed on 29 percent.

claims.text: Only about a third of herds that bought cattle isolated them from the main herd for three weeks.
claims.passage: Thirty-four percent of herds that had bought cattle in the previous year kept them apart from the main herd for at least three weeks
claims.interpretation: Isolation of purchased cattle is a realistic first target.

claims.text: Facilitated planning visits with three farm-specific priorities increased observed adoption more than usual advice at 12 months.
claims.passage: observed adoption rose by a mean of 2.1 of 12 measures in planning herds against 0.8 in usual-advice herds
claims.interpretation: The change strategy has randomised support; the local question is how to deliver it in this practice.

claims.text: Farmers said they would act on two or three priorities agreed for their farm but not on a long generic list.
claims.passage: Several farmers said they would act on two or three priorities agreed for their farm but not on a list of fifteen.
claims.interpretation: Keep the plan to a few agreed priorities.

claims.text: Farmer-reported isolation of purchased cattle greatly overstated observed isolation.
claims.passage: Farmers reported isolating purchased cattle on 61 percent of farms, but isolation facilities in use were observed on 29 percent.
claims.interpretation: Adoption must be observed, not asked.

synthesis: Five retrieved records, appraised at abstract level; the search returned few hits. Biosecurity adoption on dairy farms is low, with isolation of purchased cattle practised by about a third of herds that buy stock. One cluster-randomised trial found that a vet-facilitated plan with three farm-specific priorities raised observed adoption more than usual advice, and farmers describe acting on a few agreed priorities rather than generic lists. Farmer report overstates practice, so adoption must be observed.
gradeRationale: One moderate-quality trial in volunteer practices supports facilitated planning; the rest is observational or qualitative with self-report bias and indirectness to this practice.
summary: Five retrieved records appraised; four source-derived claims; overall certainty low.
